description.text: Murphy USA Inc. ("Murphy USA", the "Company", "we", "us", or "our") was incorporated in Delaware on March 1, 2013 and holds, through its subsidiaries, the former U.S. retail marketing business of its former parent company, Murphy Oil Corporation (“Murphy Oil”), plus other assets and liabilities of Murphy Oil that supported the activities of the U.S. retail marketing operations. In addition, on January 29, 2021, the Company acquired Quick Chek Corporation ("QuickChek" or "QC"), a privately held convenience store chain. Our business consists primarily of the marketing of retail motor fuel products and convenience merchandise through a network of 1,800 retail stores located in 27 states, of which 1,649 were branded as Murphy stores and 151 were branded as QuickChek stores. The majority of our existing and new-to-industry ("NTI") retail gasoline stores operate under the brand names of Murphy USA and Murphy Express. Plans are underway to transition all existing Murphy Express branded stores to the Murphy USA brand name. These locations operate within close proximity to Walmart stores or within preferred markets across 25 states in the Southeast, Southwest, and Midwest regions of the United States. We also operate a combination of convenience stores and convenience stores with retail gasoline located in New Jersey and New York under the brand name of QuickChek and comprises our Northeast region.

about.description_short: Murphy USA (NYSE: MUSA) is a leading retailer of gasoline and convenience merchandise with more than 1,800 stores located primarily in the Southwest, Southeast, Midwest and Northeast United States. The Company and its team of approximately 16,900 employees serve an estimated two million customers each day through its network of retail gasoline and convenience stores in 27 states. The majority of Murphy USA's stores are located in close proximity to Walmart Supercenters, but we also operate standalone stores that market gasoline and other products under the Murphy USA , Murphy Express, and QuickChek brands. Murphy USA ranks 263 among Fortune 500 companies.

employees.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, Murphy USA had approximately 16,900 employees, including 5,900 full-time employees and 11,000 part-time employees working at our stores, National Contact Center, and corporate headquarters.

analysis_md:
# Murphy USA Inc. (MUSA) — owner's-earnings DCF, pass 1

Run date 2026-10-20 · Engine 5.5.0 · Price $542.74 (Nasdaq quote API) · Market cap $10,597.5M
(19,526,000 diluted shares; cover-page count 18,380,347 as of 2026-06-30) · SIC 5500,
retail gasoline stations & convenience stores.

## What it is

Murphy USA operates ~1,806 gasoline stations with small-format convenience stores,
mostly in the South, Southeast and Midwest, many adjacent to Walmart Supercenters.
The model is low-cost, high-volume fuel retail: everyday-low fuel prices pull traffic,
merchandise (heavily nicotine) converts it. Q2 2026 (reported Aug 5, 2026): net income
$209.1M, EPS $11.27 (+53% YoY), total fuel contribution 40.6 cpg vs 32.0 cpg a year
earlier, retail gallons +3.9% (same-store +0.5%), merchandise contribution $227.4M
(+4.0%). Management guides H2 2026 at a 35 cpg all-in fuel margin, implying FY2026
net income of ~$636M and Adjusted EBITDA of ~$1.25B; same-store fuel volumes are
guided down 3% to down 1% for the year.

## Owner's earnings

Conservative OE = OCF − capex − SBC. FY2025: OCF $813.9M − capex $439.6M
(PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets, the single capex tag every year) − SBC $28.6M
(AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense) = $345.7M, or $17.70/share. The maintenance
definition (net-income based) prints $434.0M for FY2025; the score uses the
conservative definition. Per-share OE, last 3 FY: FY2023 $19.53, FY2024 $17.59,
FY2025 $17.70 — median $17.70/share (base_oe_normalized_per_share).

**Base used: TTM $27.58/share (base_source ttm_json)**, because the FY ended
2025-12-31 is 10 months stale (STALE_FY) and H1 2026 earnings power stepped up with
fuel margins. TTM legs from ttm.json (FY2025 − H1 2025 + H1 2026): OCF
$813.9M − $383.6M + $555.0M = $985.3M; capex $439.6M − $205.8M + $210.0M = $443.8M;
SBC $28.6M − $9.1M + $8.3M = $27.8M; TTM OE $513.7M over 18,628,000 diluted shares
(current-YTD count) = $27.58/share. The TTM level is corroborated by guidance:
FY2026 net income guided to ~$636M vs $470.6M in FY2025, with the H2 assumption
(35 cpg) already below Q2's print (40.6 cpg). It is not spike-free — see
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE / method range below — so probabilities are skewed bear-ward
(15/25/30/20/10) and confidence is low.

## MOAT — 5/10 (CAP 8.5 years)

Evidence: roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) FY2021–FY2025: 19.4%, 30.9%, 24.9%, 21.7%,
20.0% — above the cost of capital through strong and weak fuel-margin years.
Operating margin is thin by construction: 3.7% FY2025, 4.3% TTM. (The
fundamentals.json gross-margin series is not meaningful here — its COGS tag captures
merchandise cost only, not fuel cost — so margin evidence is quoted on operating
margin and cents-per-gallon fuel contribution instead.)

FOR: structural low-cost/high-volume model with per-store fuel volumes well above
the industry average; Walmart-adjacent "shadow anchor" sites that deliver prime
traffic without paying to generate it; scale fuel supply with RIN monetization
(5.5 cpg of Q2 2026 contribution); ROIC in double digits every year of the last
decade (13.2%–30.9% across FY2016–FY2025); disciplined buybacks
(share count −6.6%/yr, $438.9M TTM, $2B of additional authorization).

AGAINST: a commodity product with zero switching costs — customers buy on price and
location; the fuel margin itself is market-set and volatile (RIN revenue more than
doubled in Q2 2026 to $124.8M and management calls that timing, not run-rate);
secular gallon decline (2026 same-store volumes guided −3% to −1%, EV/efficiency
erosion beyond); merchandise profit concentrated in nicotine; a ~4% operating
margin leaves little buffer when margins normalize.

## Five scenarios (probs 15/25/30/20/10, mults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25)

Growth starts were recalibrated off the engine blend (−0.2%), which is an artifact:
the revenue CAGRs are pump-price effects (revenue fell FY2023–FY2025 as fuel prices
fell, while gallons grew) and the OE/share CAGR straddles the FY2022 margin spike.
Every start sits below the latest prints (Q2 EPS +53% YoY; TTM OE/share +49.6% YoY
per fundamentals.json) for a written reason: those prints are a fuel-margin and RIN
spike on a base that already capitalizes the higher level — management's own H2
guide assumes 35 cpg against Q2's 40.6 cpg. Starts are built from ~2%/yr store
growth plus buyback shrinkage, minus guided same-store gallon decline. (The
super-bear start printed at −10.0%; a deeper normalization start was floored there
by the engine.)

| Scenario | Prob | g start | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −10.0% | $100.43 | 4.5% |
| Bear | 25% | −6.0% | $142.62 | 5.5% |
| Base | 30% | +2.0% | $221.50 | 7.6% |
| Bull | 20% | +6.0% | $287.71 | 9.3% |
| Super bull | 10% | +11.0% | $401.84 | 12.0% |

**Weighted: IRR 7.44%, IV@15 $214.89** (IV@20 $153.61, IV@25 $119.56). Bear→bull IRR
band 5.5%–9.3%. Diagnostics: OE yield 5.08%, terminal value 17.8% of IV@15, upside
at 15% −60.4%. Even the super bull (10%) does not clear 15% at $542.74.

## FLAGS

- **STALE_FY** — FY2025 ended 10 months before the run. Resolved with ttm.py:
  TTM OE $513.7M / $27.58 per share (legs quoted above); the final run passes
  `--ttm` and base_source is ttm_json.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** — diluted share count shrinking 6.6%/yr (39.6M in FY2016 to
  19.5M in FY2025; 18.4M outstanding at 2026-06-30). TTM buybacks $438.9M with $2B
  of additional authorization remaining. The engine's +5pp share-count adjustment
  is already inside the growth blend; scenario starts were set from store/volume
  fundamentals and not raised again for buybacks, so there is no double count.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** — net income vs OCF: FY2024 $502.5M vs $847.6M (gap
  $345.1M); FY2025 $470.6M vs $813.9M (gap $343.3M). No one-off: D&A of $248.0M
  (FY2024) / $276.8M (FY2025) plus SBC explains most of both gaps, with working
  capital the remainder (delta_nwc −$82.7M in FY2024, +$36.6M in FY2025). It is
  structural for an asset-heavy retailer, and it does not flatter the OE base:
  capex ($458.1M / $439.6M) exceeds D&A in both years, so conservative OE charges
  more than depreciation. Capex/D&A FY2025 = 1.59× — no CAPEX_COVERAGE_LOW.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** — super-bull IV@15 is 4.0× super-bear ($401.84 vs
  $100.43). Fuel-margin uncertainty is genuinely this wide; confidence is low.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** — balance sheet at FY2025 from the filing (financials_history.csv):
  total debt $2,182.6M (noncurrent $2,163.6M plus a $19.0M current portion), cash
  $28.9M, net debt $2,153.7M, plus operating lease liabilities of $560.4M that the
  engine's net debt excludes. Net debt is 4.0× the normalized OE on this TTM-pinned
  run (6.2× the FY2025 median-base OE total of $345.7M). Against guided FY2026
  Adjusted EBITDA of ~$1.25B gross leverage is ~1.7×, and in May 2026 the company
  issued $500M of notes due 2034 to retire $300M of 2027 notes — manageable, but
  after capex the OE cushion over the debt stack is thin, which is why the bear
  cases carry negative starts and a 0.90/0.75 OE multiplier.

## Thoughts / method range

The verdict does not hinge on the base choice. On the FY-median base ($17.70/share,
preliminary run, default scenarios) the weighted IRR was 5.7% with IV@15 $139.64;
on the TTM base used here it is 7.4% with IV@15 $214.89. The method range is
**Tier D either way**. What the price needs is the 2026 fuel-margin environment —
40 cpg contribution, doubled RIN revenue — to be the permanent new level *and* to
compound; the company's own H2 guide (35 cpg) already steps down from it.

## Verdict

**Tier D.** A genuinely good operator — ~20% ROIC through the cycle, real cost
advantage, aggressive buybacks — priced at $542.74 for a fuel-margin spike its own
guidance does not extrapolate. It clears Andrew's 15% hurdle only below ~$215
(IV@15), 20% below ~$154, 25% below ~$120. Sized to the conservative end: no action
at this price.
